items.title: Three inclusions describing the commutator of the algebra O in terms of the ideal generated by AB minus BA
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes three inclusions relating the commutator subspace of the algebra O to the two-sided ideal generated by [A,B], and to its behaviour under multiplication by the central element gamma (statement lines 3049-3064). The first clause is proved by a quotient argument: dividing by O[A,B]O makes the generating pair A, B commute, so the quotient is commutative and the canonical map annihilates every commutator (proof lines 3066-3079). The second clause computes both sides of the alternating-presentation relation, whose right-hand side is a nonzero scalar multiple of [A,B] gamma while the left-hand side is visibly a sum of commutators (proof lines 3081-3092). The third clause then combines the two with the centrality of gamma in a single line. The content is in the first two clauses, each of which is an honest short argument rather than a citation. H2.
